paragraphs: The monster is following you.
You have to cross a bridge to survive.
The angry monster will catch up with you in 17 minutes.
Each member of your group moves at a different speed.
You are the fastest.
You can cross the bridge in just 1 minute.
The archer needs 2 minutes to cross, and the knight needs 5 minutes.
The wizard is the slowest.
She needs 10 minutes to cross.
You need to remember a few things.
It is so dark that you need the light from the magic stone to cross the bridge.
The bridge is not very strong, so only two of you can cross safely at a time.
All of you must reach the other side of the bridge in 17 minutes.
If you all get there, you can cut the ropes.
This way, the monster cannot follow you.
How can everyone cross the bridge in 17 minutes?
The answer is on the next page.
Take a moment to think before you check the answer.
Have you figured it out?
Then turn the page.
Here is the solution.
First, you and the archer take the stone and cross together.
It takes 2 minutes.
You come back alone with the stone in just 1 minute.
Now, 3 minutes have passed.
Next, the knight and the wizard take the stone and cross the bridge in 10 minutes.
Now, 13 minutes have passed.
Only 4 minutes are left, and you are on the starting side.
Now the archer takes the stone and returns to you in 2 minutes.
15 minutes have passed.
Finally, you and the archer cross together in 2 minutes.
That is it!
Now everyone is on the other side!
You quickly cut the ropes of the bridge.
Everyone is safe, and the magic stone is yours!

paragraphs: Art class was over, but Vashti still sat in her chair.
Her paper was blank.
Her teacher leaned over and looked at it.
“Ah! It’s a polar bear in a snowstorm,” she said.
“That’s funny!” said Vashti. “I CAN’T draw!”
Her teacher smiled. “Just make a mark.”
Vashti picked up a marker and drew a small dot on the paper.
“Here!” she said.
Her teacher picked up the paper and looked at it carefully.
“Hmmmm.”
She pushed the paper toward Vashti and asked her to sign it.
Vashti thought for a moment.
“Well, maybe I can’t draw, but I CAN sign my name.”
The next day, Vashti was surprised to see something in a frame on the wall of the art classroom.
It was her little dot!
“I can make a better dot than that!” Vashti said.
She got a brush and started painting.
A red dot. A purple dot. A yellow dot. A blue dot.
Then she mixed blue and yellow together.
She discovered that she could make a green dot.
Vashti kept experimenting.
She painted lots of little dots in many colors.
“If I can make little dots, I can make big dots, too.”
All of the dots that she painted looked beautiful together on the paper.
At the school art show a few weeks later, everyone loved Vashti’s paintings.
A little boy looked up at her.
“You’re a really great artist.”
“I want to paint like you,” he said.
“I bet you can,” said Vashti.
“Me? No, not me. I CAN’T draw!”
Vashti smiled.
She handed the boy a blank sheet of paper and told him to draw a line.
The pencil which the boy held shook as he drew.
Vashti looked at the boy’s line.
And then she said: “Sign it.”

paragraphs: After a nine-hour flight, my family finally arrived at the international airport in Honolulu.
When we came through the gate, I heard someone calling my name.
My cousin Soobin and her family were waiting for us.
When we saw each other, we hugged and jumped together in a circle.
Then Soobin put a pretty flower necklace around my neck.
She called it a lei and said that “lei” means “warm welcome.”
We visited Diamond Head first.
It is a famous hiking place.
My uncle told us how it got its name.
In the past, people mistook its shiny rocks for diamonds.
So, they named the place Diamond Head.
How interesting!
The view from the top was amazing.
Soobin and I took many pictures there!
Today we went to a culture center.
We learned about traditional Hawaiian culture there.
First, we learned what some Hawaiian words mean.
“Aloha” is used to say “hello” or “goodbye,” and “mahalo” means “thank you.”
Then it was hula dance time!
Surprisingly, many of the movements stood for things in nature.
For example, if you raise your arms above your head in a circle, it stands for the moon.
When I danced hula, I could feel the Hawaiian people’s love for nature.
On the way back to Soobin’s house, we saw a big, beautiful rainbow.
Soobin explained, “You can often see rainbows in Hawaii. So, Hawaii is called the Rainbow State.”
Today, we headed to Hanauma Bay to go snorkeling.
Before snorkeling, we watched an educational video.
We learned not to harm the sea animals or touch the coral.
The underwater world was wonderful.
We saw lots of colorful fish and a turtle swimming there.
It was amazing!
It is already the last day of our trip.
I’m sad to go home, but I will always remember Hawaii.
Aloha, Soobin! Mahalo, Hawaii!!

sentences.en: After a nine-hour flight, my family finally arrived at the international airport in Honolulu.
sentences.ko: 9시간의 비행 후에 / 우리 가족은 마침내 도착했다 / 호놀룰루의 국제공항에.

sentences.en: When we came through the gate, I heard someone calling my name.
sentences.ko: 우리가 게이트를 통과했을 때 / 나는 들었다 / 누군가가 내 이름을 부르는 것을.

sentences.en: My cousin Soobin and her family were waiting for us.
sentences.ko: 내 사촌 수빈이와 그녀의 가족은 / 우리를 기다리고 있었다.

sentences.en: When we saw each other, we hugged and jumped together in a circle.
sentences.ko: 우리가 서로를 보았을 때 / 우리는 껴안았다 / 그리고 함께 뛰었다 / 원을 이루며.

sentences.en: Then Soobin put a pretty flower necklace around my neck.
sentences.ko: 그다음 수빈이는 놓았다 / 예쁜 꽃목걸이를 / 내 목 둘레에.

sentences.en: She called it a lei and said that “lei” means “warm welcome.”
sentences.ko: 그녀는 그것을 레이라고 불렀다 / 그리고 말했다 / ‘lei’가 ‘따뜻한 환영’을 의미한다고.

sentences.en: We visited Diamond Head first.
sentences.ko: 우리는 다이아몬드 헤드를 방문했다 / 먼저.

sentences.en: It is a famous hiking place.
sentences.ko: 그곳은 / 유명한 하이킹 장소이다.

sentences.en: My uncle told us how it got its name.
sentences.ko: 내 삼촌은 우리에게 알려 주었다 / 그것이 어떻게 그 이름을 얻게 되었는지.

sentences.en: In the past, people mistook its shiny rocks for diamonds.
sentences.ko: 과거에 / 사람들은 착각했다 / 그곳의 반짝이는 바위들을 / 다이아몬드로.

sentences.en: So, they named the place Diamond Head.
sentences.ko: 그래서 / 그들은 그 장소의 이름을 지었다 / 다이아몬드 헤드라고.

sentences.en: How interesting!
sentences.ko: 정말 흥미롭다!

sentences.en: The view from the top was amazing.
sentences.ko: 정상에서의 경치는 / 놀라웠다.

sentences.en: Soobin and I took many pictures there!
sentences.ko: 수빈이와 나는 / 많은 사진을 찍었다 / 그곳에서!

sentences.en: Today we went to a culture center.
sentences.ko: 오늘 우리는 갔다 / 문화 센터에.

sentences.en: We learned about traditional Hawaiian culture there.
sentences.ko: 우리는 배웠다 / 전통적인 하와이 문화에 대해 / 그곳에서.

sentences.en: First, we learned what some Hawaiian words mean.
sentences.ko: 먼저 / 우리는 배웠다 / 몇몇 하와이 단어들이 무엇을 의미하는지.

sentences.en: “Aloha” is used to say “hello” or “goodbye,” and “mahalo” means “thank you.”
sentences.ko: ‘Aloha’는 사용된다 / ‘안녕’ 또는 ‘잘 가’를 말하는 데 / 그리고 ‘mahalo’는 ‘고맙습니다’를 의미한다.

sentences.en: Then it was hula dance time!
sentences.ko: 그다음은 / 훌라 춤 시간이었다!

sentences.en: Surprisingly, many of the movements stood for things in nature.
sentences.ko: 놀랍게도 / 많은 동작들은 상징했다 / 자연 속의 것들을.

sentences.en: For example, if you raise your arms above your head in a circle, it stands for the moon.
sentences.ko: 예를 들어 / 만약 네가 팔을 들어 올리면 / 머리 위로 원 모양으로 / 그것은 달을 상징한다.

sentences.en: When I danced hula, I could feel the Hawaiian people’s love for nature.
sentences.ko: 내가 훌라를 췄을 때 / 나는 느낄 수 있었다 / 하와이 사람들의 자연에 대한 사랑을.

sentences.en: On the way back to Soobin’s house, we saw a big, beautiful rainbow.
sentences.ko: 수빈이의 집으로 돌아가는 길에 / 우리는 보았다 / 크고 아름다운 무지개를.

sentences.en: Soobin explained, “You can often see rainbows in Hawaii. So, Hawaii is called the Rainbow State.”
sentences.ko: 수빈이가 설명했다 / ‘너는 하와이에서 무지개를 자주 볼 수 있어 / 그래서 하와이는 불린다 / 무지개 주라고.’

sentences.en: Today, we headed to Hanauma Bay to go snorkeling.
sentences.ko: 오늘 / 우리는 향했다 / 하나우마 베이로 / 스노클링을 하러.

sentences.en: Before snorkeling, we watched an educational video.
sentences.ko: 스노클링하기 전에 / 우리는 보았다 / 교육용 영상을.

sentences.en: We learned not to harm the sea animals or touch the coral.
sentences.ko: 우리는 배웠다 / 바다 동물들을 해치지 말고 / 산호를 만지지 말라고.

sentences.en: The underwater world was wonderful.
sentences.ko: 바닷속 세계는 / 멋졌다.

sentences.en: We saw lots of colorful fish and a turtle swimming there.
sentences.ko: 우리는 보았다 / 많은 형형색색의 물고기들과 거북이 한 마리가 / 그곳에서 헤엄치는 것을.

sentences.en: It was amazing!
sentences.ko: 그것은 / 놀라웠다!

sentences.en: It is already the last day of our trip.
sentences.ko: 벌써 / 우리 여행의 마지막 날이다.

sentences.en: I’m sad to go home, but I will always remember Hawaii.
sentences.ko: 나는 집에 가게 되어 슬프다 / 하지만 나는 언제나 하와이를 기억할 것이다.

sentences.en: Aloha, Soobin! Mahalo, Hawaii!!
sentences.ko: 알로하, 수빈! / 마할로, 하와이!
